title: The scheduled() handler opens against the elicited cron triggers on boot and emits cronReady
asA: developer whose Worker needs to schedule work on a cron cadence behind a swappable boundary
iWant: one scheduled() handler module to hold the Cron Trigger event reference, wire the dispatcher and the event sink, and emit a cronReady lifecycle event on the first successful ready-check
soThat: the boundary between my domain and the vendor's scheduled seam is the only place that has to move when the dispatcher shape changes, and boot ordering is observable via the event

acceptanceCriteria.description: On process boot, the scheduled handler binds against the elicited cron triggers (the [triggers] crons block in wrangler.toml on the fixture), wires the dispatcher and the injected sink; the ready() call fires cronReady on the sink with a payload of exactly {event, expression, scheduledTime, outcome, duration} per TAC-3303 where expression is null, scheduledTime is null, outcome is 'ready' and duration is 0. The scheduled handler module (src/scheduled.mjs) does NOT dereference env.CACHE (the KV binding) or any other env binding; a source-tree grep of that file returns zero hits for env.CACHE.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a Node or Worker process with the scheduled handler module imported and its factory invoked with the elicited configuration
acceptanceCriteria.when: the process boots and the scheduled handler ready() call resolves
acceptanceCriteria.then: a cronReady event fires on the injected sink carrying the cron-vocabulary metadata payload {event, expression, scheduledTime, outcome, duration}; the scheduled.mjs source has zero env.CACHE references

acceptanceCriteria.description: createScheduledHandler({routes: []}) throws a named error kind CRON_HANDLER_INVALID_ROUTES before any binding is dereferenced; no cronReady event fires on the sink. Same for routes omitted or routes not an array.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a call to createScheduledHandler with routes as an empty array (or not an array at all)
acceptanceCriteria.then: the factory throws CRON_HANDLER_INVALID_ROUTES and no event is emitted on the sink

acceptanceCriteria.description: createScheduledHandler called with the sink argument not a function (per TAC-3303) throws a named error kind CRON_HANDLER_INVALID_SINK before any binding is dereferenced.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a call to createScheduledHandler with the sink argument not a function
acceptanceCriteria.then: the factory throws CRON_HANDLER_INVALID_SINK and no event is emitted

acceptanceCriteria.description: Repeat-boot idempotency: two sequential createScheduledHandler(...).ready() calls emit two cronReady records on the sink, both with identical shape {event:"cronReady", expression:null, scheduledTime:null, outcome:"ready", duration:0}. No accumulator drift; no shared state leaks between instances.
acceptanceCriteria.given: two independent createScheduledHandler instances constructed with identical arguments
acceptanceCriteria.when: ready() is called on each in turn
acceptanceCriteria.then: the sink receives two cronReady records with identical payload shape

acceptanceCriteria.description: Sole-reader source-tree scan: a recursive scan of the cf-platform fixture src/ tree greps every .mjs file for the substrings "event?.cron", "event.cron" and "event?.scheduledTime"; the only file carrying these tokens is src/scheduled.mjs. Any other module carrying the raw Cron Trigger event field access surfaces as a leak with the file path.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the cf-platform fixture src/ tree and the sole-reader scan probe
acceptanceCriteria.when: the scan walks every .mjs file matching the token list
acceptanceCriteria.then: the only file with matches is src/scheduled.mjs; every other file returns zero matches

acceptanceCriteria.description: The applied blueprint's manifest declares the `scheduledTrigger` capability token and the applied project ships the single scheduled() handler module per AC-32101-1; therefore the `scheduledTrigger` promise the manifest carries is backed by the live handler the deployed Worker registers.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the applied blueprint manifest at `blueprints/platform-cloudflare-cron-triggers/blueprint.json` and the applied fixture with the shipped scheduled() handler module
acceptanceCriteria.when: the anatomy test reads the blueprint manifest and asserts the handler module presence per AC-32101-1
acceptanceCriteria.then: the manifest carries `scheduledTrigger` on its `capabilities[]` list and the applied handler module is present, so `scheduledTrigger` is a live promise the applying project can act on
